title: Separate 90% wind bands covered the full 24–72 h path in 76% of selected NHC cases in two basins in 2019–2025
abstract: We tested joint wind uncertainty for official NHC forecasts in two basins. Separate 90% Gaussian bands used the previous five years of errors at each lead. In 2019–2025, the bands covered all 24, 48 and 72 h errors in 75.7% of 1,202 Atlantic cycles and 75.8% of 756 East Pacific cycles. Scaling by past maximum errors raised coverage to 90.8% and 87.3%. A fixed Gaussian Bonferroni scale gave 89.7% and 88.6%. The fitted scale had greater quantile loss than the fixed scale in the Atlantic: difference +0.00316, with 95% storm limits +0.00060 to +0.00562. The East Pacific difference was uncertain. Thus this test did not support a general gain from the fitted scale over the fixed comparator. Mean band widths, other horizons, earlier years, history checks and year resampling show the scope of the result. These are reconstructed research bands, not probabilities issued by NHC. Complete-case selection, revised best-track records, changing forecast systems and fixed-fit uncertainty limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and an independent arithmetic check support reproduction. Raw and cycle-level source extracts remain external.

display.caption: Joint coverage and mean band widths for selected NHC forecast cycles in 2019–2025. Limits resample whole storms and hold historical fits fixed.

citations.reason: Extends its single-time intensity bands to a joint event.
Extends its joint track score design to signed wind errors and adds a fixed comparator.
